thread:
micah: Quick check — I'm proposing a small CB heuristic tweak: pick smaller max_batch for short-sequence requests but allow larger batches for long completions. Planning a throughput sweep tomorrow on staging. Anyone object?

sara: +1. What's our threshold for 'short'? 128 tokens?

devin: For chat I'd lean 64 as 'short', 128 for single-shot completions. Also need to cap queue timeout so we don't blow latency SLOs.

micah: Thinking heuristics like: if median_seq_len < 80 -> max_batch=32, max_tokens_cap=256; else max_batch=128, max_tokens_cap=512. And allow per-route overrides.

jonathan: Can we make it reactive to recent latency (p95)? e.g. if p95 > 200ms, reduce batch cap automatically. That'll help degradation during spikes.

aisha: Agree. Also we need distinction between warm vs cold KV cache — cold KV will spike compute and change the optimal batch sizes.

micah: Plan: do a 30m dry-run with loadgen + kv-cold flag, then a warm run. Sweep dims: max_batch in [32,64,128], max_tokens_cap in [128,256,512], queue_ms in [5,15,50]. Capture throughput, p50/p95 latency, token-cost.

devin: I'll run the warm/cold experiments. Which cluster? staging-cb or canary-prod?

micah: staging-cb first. If results look sane, we'll promote to canary-prod for a short smoke. Need someone to watch the SLO dashboard during canary.

sara: I'll watch SLOs and error budget. Ping me 09:15 PST when canary starts.

jonathan: Also add a tracing span for queue-wait so we can measure head-of-line latency. Minimal patch suggestion:

```
metrics.histogram("cb.queue_wait_ms", queue_wait_ms)
```

micah: Added that to PR #4238 and created a small span around queue wait. @devin @jonathan — requesting review.

devin: Reviewing now. Quick nit: prefer generic name "cb.queue_wait_ms" as histogram but expose percentiles in console; don't hardcode p95 in metric name.

micah: Good catch, updated PR and docstring. PR now includes rollout notes and per-route override examples.

bench-bot: loadtest scheduled: 2026-03-18T16:00Z, id=lt-778. Test config attached to the loadtest run.

aisha: Heads-up: if we tighten max_tokens_cap too much we may see quality regressions for long-context completions. Add prompt-based regression evals after each sweep.

micah: Will attach the eval suite and run it automatically post-sweep. We'll check rouge/bertscore + simple pass/fail on golden prompts.

sara: OK — run approved. Devin and Aisha to own rollback procedure if regressions or SLO violations appear. Micah will coordinate the rollout window.

devin: noted, I'll be by my laptop during the loadtest.

micah: Thanks all — I'll post a short summary of staging results in this thread after the dry-run. :thumbsup:
